معتمدا على اللمس والشم.. ضرير يحضر وجبة "الربيس" في المهرة. يعتمد سالمين عويضان في مديرية المسيلة بمحافظة المهرة شرقي اليمن على حاستي اللمس والشم لإعداد وجبة "الربيس" التراثية رغم فقدانه البصر منذ سنوات طويلة.

متهمون بالخيانة عند الفشل.. لماذا لا يشارك اللاعبون في اختيار المدربين؟. بعد رحيل 11 مدربا في موسم واحد، يبرز سؤال غير مألوف في الدوري الإنجليزي: هل يملك اللاعبون ما يؤهلهم للمشاركة في اختيار مدربيهم؟

حزب الأصالة والمعاصرة يتصدر النتائج الأولية للانتخابات التشريعية في المغرب. أعلنت الداخلية المغربية تصدر حزب الأصالة والمعاصرة النتائج الأولية للانتخابات التشريعية بـ97 مقعدا، تلاه التجمع الوطني للأحرار بـ66 مقعدا.

هآرتس: المقاطعة الأوروبية تضرب إمدادات الجيش الإسرائيلي. كشفت صحيفة هآرتس الإسرائيلية عن إقرار الجيش بتأثير المقاطعة الأوروبية على عمليات إمداداته، خصوصا في سلاح البحرية، خلافا لتصريحات المستوى السياسي الإسرائيلي.

بين الموضة والسياسة.. جدل في إيطاليا بشأن غياب ميلوني عن الجمعية العامة. أثار غياب جورجا ميلوني عن الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة وحضورها أسبوع الموضة بميلانو جدلاً في إيطاليا، وسط انتقادات المعارضة وتكهنات بشأن الأسباب إذ ترجح صحيفة إيطالية أن السبب هو توتر علاقتها بترمب.

تحقيق في اختفاء غامض لمكونات إف-35.. هل تسربت أسرار المقاتلة إلى الصين؟. تحقق أستراليا والولايات المتحدة بشأن اختفاء شحنة مكونات من برنامج مقاتلات إف-35 في المحيط الهادي، حيث يُخشى أمريكيا أن تكون وصلت إلى الصين.

من أعدها ولماذا لم تُنشر؟.. وثيقة أمريكية تندد ببريطانيا وفرنسا وكندا. تتهم مذكرة أمريكية -وفقا لوكالة رويترز- فرنسا وبريطانيا وكندا بتبني خطط مستمدة من إستراتيجيات معادية للسامية، على خلفية العقوبات المعلنة ضد سياسة إسرائيل في الضفة الغربية.

"فنزويلا تولد من جديد".. رودريغيز تتعهد بانتخابات أمام الأمم المتحدة وتشيد بترمب. قالت رئيسة فنزويلا بالوكالة إن انتخابات ستجري في البلاد بعد التطورات الأخيرة التي عرفتها فنزويلا، عقب اعتقال الرئيس السابق نيكولاس مادورو في عملية عسكرية أمريكية.

عام دراسي جديد على وقع الحرب.. بزشكيان يقرع الجرس وطلاب إيران يترقبون. مع عودة أكثر من 16.5 مليون طالب إلى المدارس، تكشف شهادات معلم وطلاب بالثانوية أن ذكرى الحرب وغموض اختبار القبول الجامعي وارتفاع كلفة الدراسة تلقي بظلال ثقيلة على بداية العام الدراسي في إيران.

سي إن إن: 8 محاولات انتحار فوق حاملة الطائرات "لينكولن" قبالة إيران. كشف تقرير لـ"سي إن إن" عن تواتر محاولات الانتحار بين أفراد البحرية الأمريكية فوق حاملة الطائرات "يو إس إس أبراهام لينكولن" التي شاركت في مهمة قتالية بالشرق الأوسط ضد إيران.

قراصنة يزعمون سرقة بيانات آلاف عملاء "إف بي آي" والمكتب يحقق. تعرضت بوابة وظائف "إف بي آي" لاختراق من قبل مجموعة قراصنة تزعم سرقة بيانات آلاف الموظفين والمتقدمين، بينها عناوين وأرقام ومعلومات عائلية وطبية، وقد بدأ المكتب التحقيق في حجم الاختراق ومصدره ومخاطره.

التوتر يتصاعد.. باكستان تعلن استهداف 10 مواقع في أفغانستان. أعلنت باكستان عن توجيه ضربات "دقيقة" ضد عشرة مواقع داخل أفغانستان "دفاعا عن النفس"، فيما نفذت اليوم الخميس غارة على مدينة قندهار، وفق ما ذكرت تقارير.

عالقون بسبب أزمة السكن وجبل متصدع يهدد الآلاف في كابل. مئات العائلات القاطنة بمنطقة "چهلستون" جنوب العاصمة الأفغانية تلقوا تحذيرات من انهيارات خطيرة، لكنهم لا يملكون المال ولا البديل في ظل أزمة السكن.

"احتفل وحيدا فانتفض له الشعب".. ما قصة العريس صالح "يتيم مروانة" في الجزائر؟. تحول زفاف الشاب الجزائري "يتيم مروانة" من ليلة حزينة خالية من الحضور إلى ملحمة تضامن حاشدة، عقب توافد المئات من مختلف الولايات لمشاركته الفرحة وتقديم الدعم والهدايا.

وسط توترات تجارية وتكنولوجية.. شي يدعو من واشنطن للتكامل لا الخصومة مع أمريكا. أكد الرئيس الصيني في واشنطن ضرورة الشراكة مع أمريكا لا الخصومة، متطلعا لمباحثات مع ترمب تشمل ملفات التجارة والذكاء الاصطناعي وإيران بحضور كبار قادة التكنولوجيا.

الحكومة السودانية ترفض تشكيك أمريكا في شرعيتها. أعلن السودان، الأربعاء، أنه "يتمسك بسيادته الوطنية" ودعا واشنطن إلى التعامل بشكل إيجابي مع الحكومة وذلك ردا على بيان صادر عن وزارة الخارجية الأمريكية شكك في شرعيتها.
شاهد البث المباشر لتلفزيون بي بي سي
هل تؤثر مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي على علاقاتنا العاطفية؟. هل تؤثر مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي والمحتوى الذي نستهلكه عن العلاقات العاطفية في الطريقة التي نعيش بها علاقاتنا؟

من صواريخ اليمن إلى حرب السودان: كيف يُستخدم الذكاء الاصطناعي في صراعات المنطقة؟. من محاولات تطوير أسلحة في اليمن إلى حملات تأثير مرتبطة بحرب السودان، واستخدامات استخباراتية في غزة ولبنان، ترصد تقارير أوجهاً متعددة لاستخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي في النزاعات. ماذا تقول المصادر، وما ردود الأطراف المعنية؟
صور تُظهر أضراراً واسعة في مواقع أمريكية بدول عربية جرّاء هجمات إيرانية. طائرة عسكرية محطمة ومبانٍ مدمرة تظهر في صور حصلت عليها شبكة "سي بي إس نيوز"، الشريك الأمريكي لبي بي سي.

كيف غيّرت انفجارات "البيجر" تاريخ إصابات العيون في الحروب؟. تأتي الذكرى الثانية لانفجارات أجهزة "البيجر" في لبنان لتفتح ملفاً طبياً وإنسانيا غير مسبوق، فبحسب دراسة حديثة أعدها فريق طبي في الجامعة الأمريكية في بيروت، فإن استهداف هذه الأجهزة أحدث دماراً بالغاً بين غير المشاركين في القتال، لا سيما النساء والأطفال.

عبد الملك الحوثي.. من هو زعيم حركة "أنصار الله" في اليمن؟. يلعب عبد الملك الحوثي، زعيم جماعة أنصار الله الحوثية، دوراً بارزاً في الحياة السياسية في اليمن. فماذا نعرف عنه؟ وما أبرز الصراعات التي انخرطت فيها الحركة تحت زعامته؟

باب المندب: كيف وصل الحوثيون إلى مكمن الضعف الإستراتيجي للسعودية؟. الهجوم الحوثي الأخير، الذي أسفر عن السيطرة على معظم الساحل الغربي لليمن المطل على البحر الأحمر والتقدم حتى مضيق باب المندب، ربما منح طهران أوراق ضغط أكبر في مواجهة واشنطن. إلا أنه يكشف أيضاً عن تنامي القدرات العسكرية والتنظيمية للجماعة نفسها، وعن المعضلة شديدة التعقيد التي تواجهها السعودية، التي تعاني أصلاً من استنزاف مواردها وتعدد التحديات التي تواجهها.

أمجد فريد في بلا قيود: اتهام أمريكا للجيش السوداني باستخدام أسلحة كيماوية في غير محله. شدّد الدكتور أمجد فريد مستشار مجلس السيادة السوداني للشؤون السياسية والعلاقات الخارجية على وجود آلية لمحاكمة من يرتكب جريمة أو انتهاكا من قِبل أي من جنود وضباط القوات المسلحة السودانية أوالقوات الموالية لها وخضوعهم أمام محاكم عسكرية أو مدنية أو إحالتهم إلى التقاعد.
لماذا تنخفض نتائج اختبارات جيل زد؟. كشفت أكبر دراسة دولية في العالم تُجرى على مراهقين في الخامسة عشرة من العمر عن انخفاض مُقلق في نتائج العلوم والرياضيات والقراءة.
إيد شيران يعتذر للحضور عن "ارتكابه الأخطاء". استهل شيران حفله في فيلادلفيا بالحديث عن الجدل الذي أحاط بالجولة منذ ذلك الحين، ودفع جميع الفنانين المشاركين في إحياء حفلاتها الافتتاحية إلى الانسحاب.

الانتخابات المغربية 2026: بين تطلعات الناخبين ووعود الأحزاب. بدأت الحملة الانتخابية في 10 سبتمبر/أيلول الجاري، وتستمر حتى منتصف ليل الثلاثاء 22 من الشهر نفسه، وسط تحديات اقتصادية واجتماعية وجيوسياسية.

جيل زد والانتخابات المغربية.. هل تكفي الوجوه الشابة لاستعادة الثقة؟. بين من فقدوا الثقة في النخب السياسية ومن يراهنون على التغيير عبر صناديق الاقتراع، يبقى السؤال: هل تنجح الأحزاب في استعادة ثقة الشباب، أم أن فجوة الثقة ستستمر؟

هل تتدخل تركيا وباكستان لحماية السعودية أمام هجمات الحوثيين؟. مع تصاعد التوترات بين السعودية والحوثيين، واستمرار الهجمات على مدن السعودية، تطرح التساؤلات حول دور "حلف مكة" في مساعدة السعودية ضد حركة أنصار الله الحوثية، فما هو موقف تركيا وباكستان من التصعيد؟

ما التحديات التي تواجه الدخول المدرسي في مناطق الصراع في العالم العربي؟. عام دراسي جديد يبدأ في العديد من المناطق التي نكبتها الحرب في العالم العربي وتساؤلات عن كيف يتأثر جيل من التلاميذ بما خلفته الحروب.

هل يمكن للعقوبات الأمريكية أن تغلق الباب أمام الرحلات الجوية الأجنبية إلى إيران؟. بينما توقفت فعلياً رحلات شركات الطيران الأجنبية إلى إيران عقب الحرب والتوترات الإقليمية، فرضت الولايات المتحدة عقوبات جديدة على قطاع الطيران الإيراني قد تجعل عودة هذه الرحلات أكثر تعقيداً وصعوبة، حتى بعد انحسار المخاطر الأمنية.

"رهان واشنطن على انتفاضة الشعب الإيراني ضد النظام الحاكم سياسة فاشلة" – في الغارديان. في عرض الصحف اليوم: كيف بدأت تتلاشى الصورة التي كانت سائدة في إيران عن "شعب اختطفته مؤسسته السياسية"، وتحذير من أن الحوثيين وضعوا أيديهم على "نقطة ضعف الغرب"، ووزير الخارجية البريطاني السابق الذي يصف البريكست بأنه "إعلان أحادي الجانب عن العجز السياسي".
ما الذي سيجري في القمة المقبلة بين ترامب والرئيس الصيني شي جينبينغ؟. قمة رئاسية جديدة بين الولايات المتحدة والصين: ما هي الملفات المطروحة على الطاولة؟

هل ترتفع أسعار الخبز في مصر؟. جدل متصاعد في مصر بشأن أسعار الخبز، والمخابز تطالب بالزيادة بعد ارتفاع أسعار الدقيق على خلفية الاضطرابات في منطقة الشرق الأوسط ومضيق هرمز.
وكالة أممية ترصد تصاعداً في تقارير العنف ضد النساء في غزة. يشير صندوق الأمم المتحدة للسكان إلى حدوث "تصعيد حاد" في أعداد حالات الزواج المبكر والقسري.

Élections au Maroc : au-delà des promesses, les défis économiques du prochain gouvernement. Au Maroc, la campagne législative se joue sur le terrain social. SMIG à 5 000 dirhams, revalorisation des retraites, création d’emplois : les partis surenchérissent face à des défis économiques qui dépassent les slogans.

ONU : comment Macky Sall a tenté d’empêcher l’accès à un site web critiquant son bilan. Le 9 septembre, le tribunal judiciaire de Paris a débouté l’ancien président du Sénégal, qui tentait de faire bloquer l’accès, depuis la France, à un site militant qui entend démontrer son « inaptitude » à la fonction de secrétaire général des Nations unies.

Côte d’Ivoire : la stratégie d’Abidjan pour encadrer le secteur de l’or. Alors que le secteur aurifère est en plein essor en Côte d’Ivoire, l’exécutif a lancé un volet de mesures pour mettre fin à l’orpaillage illégal et réglementer les mines artisanales. Un chantier aux multiples enjeux.

Côte d’Ivoire : tout comprendre au mandat d’arrêt contre Habiba Touré, proche de Laurent Gbagbo. Dévoilée par le procureur à la surprise générale, la mesure de justice visant Habiba Touré n’avait pas encore été rendue publique. Quand la Côte d’Ivoire a-t-elle saisi la France où la porte-parole du PPA-CI réside ? Risque-t-elle l’extradition ? Décryptage.

Au Sénégal, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, un président confronté à un procès en « trahison ». Depuis sa rupture avec son Premier ministre, Ousmane Sonko, dont il avait été le bras droit, le chef de l’État sénégalais est sous le feu des critiques de ses anciens alliés Pastef. Après avoir conquis le pouvoir ensemble, les deux ex-partenaires en appellent désormais au verdict des urnes.

Cameroun : la « bamiphobie », un débat qui continue de déchirer le pays. Au Cameroun, le débat sur la « bamiphobie », un terme popularisé par l’écrivain Patrice Nganang et qui désigne la discrimination des Bamilékés, continue de faire rage. L’opposant Alain Fogué l’a relancé depuis sa cellule de la prison de Kondengui.

Cameroun : comment Louis-Paul Motaze prépare le terrain en vue d’un accord avec le FMI. Nouveau programme avec le FMI, emprunt obligataire, roadshow à Londres : Yaoundé cherche des financements sur tous les fronts. Mais les conditions posées par le Fonds restent loin d’être toutes remplies.

Au Niger, l’avocat et activiste Abdourahamane Lirwana écroué après avoir évoqué les dissensions au sein de l’armée. Figure de la société civile nigérienne, Abdourahamane Lirwana a été incarcéré mardi à la prison civile de Niamey pour « diffusion de données de nature à troubler l’ordre public », après des publications sur les réseaux sociaux.

RDC : Baraka Kabemba, le consultant qui veut doper les revenus de la Gécamines. Ancien associé d’EY et familier des partenariats miniers de la Gécamines, Baraka Kabemba a pris les commandes de l’entreprise publique en mars 2026 avec l’objectif de mieux valoriser ses actifs.

Mali – États-Unis : pourquoi le soutien de l’Ukraine au FLA contrarie l’administration Trump. Des opérateurs de drones ukrainiens apportent un soutien actif aux indépendantistes du FLA et à leurs alliés du Jnim contre Assimi Goïta. Une révélation embarrassante pour Washington, théoriquement proche de Kiev mais désireux de renouer avec Bamako.

À l’ONU, la stratégie de l’administration Trump sur le Soudan provoque la colère de ses alliés. Le refus de l’administration Trump d’accorder au général Abdel Fattah al-Burhane, chef des Forces armées soudanaises, un visa pour se rendre à New York où il souhaitait assister à l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies a provoqué la colère de certains des alliés de Washington, mais aussi de l’organisation elle-même.

Monnaie de la Cedeao : le lancement de l’eco en 2027 est-il crédible ?. La Communauté économique des États d’Afrique de l’Ouest continue d’affirmer que sa monnaie unique verra le jour en 2027. Mais entre l’objectif politique et sa mise en circulation, le parcours est semé d’embûches.

Nigeria : TotalEnergies mise 800 millions de dollars sur le champ gazier d’Ima. Le géant pétrolier français a acté sa décision d’investir massivement dans un champ gazier inexploité depuis sa découverte au large de l’île de Bonny il y a près de cinquante ans. Un signal fort pour Bola Tinubu, qui veut faire du pays un hub énergétique continental.

Vodacom-Safaricom : plongée au cœur des controverses entourant la vente du fleuron kényan. La Haute Cour du Kenya a annulé la vente d’une participation de 15 % dans Safaricom à Vodacom, jugeant le processus inconstitutionnel. Un verdict qui relance le débat sur la transparence et le prix de la cession.

RDC : face à Félix Tshisekedi, l’opposition est-elle en train de perdre la bataille de la rue ?. Malgré le faible engouement suscité par sa marche du 15 septembre, la coalition C64 mise toujours sur la mobilisation populaire pour contrer le projet de changement constitutionnel. Mais sa capacité à imposer un rapport de force avec le pouvoir semble pour l’instant limitée.

L’Afrique au Conseil de sécurité : l’interminable débat sur une injustice tenace. Un continent de 1,4 milliard d’habitants sans voix décisive à l’ONU : le cri africain résonne à nouveau à New York. Mais entre discours consensuels et diplomatie du rapport de force, la réforme du Conseil de sécurité reste un vœu pieux.

Maroc : le géant OCP poursuit sa réorganisation dans un contexte de chocs géopolitiques. Quelques mois après sa réorganisation d’avril, OCP procède à de nouveaux ajustements à sa tête. Hicham El Habti hérite notamment du poste de secrétaire général. Coulisses.

Est de la RDC : entre le Rwanda et la Belgique, une réconciliation qui vient de loin. Le Rwanda avait rompu ses relations avec la Belgique le 17 mars 2025 après l’avoir accusée d’avoir pris le parti de Kinshasa dans le conflit à l’est de la RDC. Les deux pays privilégient désormais le dialogue.

Cameroun : le 24 octobre 2020, le bruit et la fureur s’abattaient sur Kumba. Le 24 octobre 2020, sept enfants étaient tués par balles dans leur salle de classe, à Kumba, dans le Sud-Ouest. Retour sur ce massacre, qui reste l’un des épisodes les plus sombres de la crise anglophone qui endeuille le Cameroun depuis dix ans.

Côte d’Ivoire : Meyliet Koné, Beugré Mambé, Birahima Ouattara, le trio au cœur du pouvoir. Vice-président, Premier ministre et vice-Premier ministre ; trois hommes, trois fonctions, une même loyauté. Alassane Ouattara a redistribué les rôles sans bousculer la hiérarchie et dispose désormais d’un premier cercle de confiance pour le seconder. Et lui succéder ?

Mines : comment la Chine a mis la main sur le lithium africain. Du Zimbabwe au Mali en passant par le Ghana et la RDC, les groupes chinois s’imposent comme les maîtres du lithium africain. Le secret de cette hégémonie : une stratégie industrielle et financière menée selon des méthodes bien éprouvées.

Au Maroc, le PAM arrive en tête des législatives et attend le choix du roi. Le PAM remporte les élections législatives marocaines avec 97 sièges, devant le RNI et l’Istiqlal, dans un Parlement où le PJD retrouve une place centrale. Le scrutin ouvre désormais la phase institutionnelle avec la nomination par le roi Mohammed VI d’un chef du gouvernement issu du parti arrivé en tête.

Au Maroc, les faux-semblants d’une campagne législative sans relief. Le scrutin du 23 septembre ne suscite que peu d’intérêt dans le royaume, où le thème du coût de la vie est la préoccupation dominante parmi les électeurs. Les partis favoris, proches du palais royal, se contentent d’une campagne de façade.

Le Consortium international des journalistes d’investigation s’inquiète de la disparition d’un de ses enquêteurs à Djibouti. Le journaliste sud-africain Micah Reddy et son fixeur local, Kooki Mahmoud, n’ont pas donné de nouvelles depuis samedi. Leur employeur redoute qu’ils aient été arrêtés par les services de sécurité djiboutiens.

Miguel Masaisai, qui traversait l’Afrique à vélo pour demander la fin de la guerre en RDC, est mort percuté par un camion. Le jeune homme, originaire de Goma, dans l’Est de la République démocratique du Congo, s’était fixé pour mission de pédaler jusqu’à Rabat, au Maroc, pour demander la fin de la guerre dans son pays. Son périple a pris fin sur une route du Congo-Brazzaville.

Vincent Brown, soupçonné d’avoir participé au génocide des Tutsi au Rwanda, devient le premier inculpé au Royaume-Uni pour ces faits. Cet homme de 65 ans, résidant à Londres, a été arrêté à l’issue d’une enquête de sept ans déclenchée par une requête officielle des autorités rwandaises.

En Afrique du Sud, les compagnies de sécurité privées font la police. Dans un pays où sévit une criminalité galopante, la moitié des victimes de cambriolage ne font pas appel aux forces de l’ordre, réputées impuissantes.

En Ethiopie, les principaux groupes armés s’allient contre le pouvoir d’Abiy Ahmed. Sept groupes de combattants issus de plusieurs régions du pays se sont coalisés autour d’un objectif commun : renverser le premier ministre.

Yémen : l’ONU prévoit 230 000 déplacés et 10 000 réfugiés à Djibouti dans les prochains mois. Les combats au Yémen ont fait 154 morts ces deux derniers jours, ont précisé à l’Agence France-Presse des sources militaires dans les deux camps.

Au Liberia, la fin de l’aide américaine fait exploser la malnutrition infantile. La fermeture de l’Agence des Etats-Unis pour le développement international, dissoute en 2025 par Donald Trump, a de graves conséquences en Afrique, notamment au Liberia, où seuls 2,4 % des enfants de moins de 2 ans bénéficient d’une alimentation minimale acceptable.

Au Maroc, un an après le mouvement de la « gen Z », la jeunesse reste la grande absente des élections législatives. S’estimant ignorés par les formations politiques et les institutions, les moins de 30 ans sont peu nombreux à se porter candidat et vont probablement exprimer leur défiance par une abstention massive aux élections du 23 septembre.

Crise migratoire à Ceuta : le premier ministre espagnol, Pedro Sanchez, estime que le contrôle des frontières par le Maroc a « échoué ». Madrid a annoncé, mardi, avoir demandé « des réponses » à Rabat après l’afflux de plus de 70 000 migrants, fin juillet, dans l’enclave espagnole située en Afrique du Nord.

Soudan du Sud : le président dissout le gouvernement à trois mois d’élections toujours incertaines. Salva Kiir avait promulgué, lundi, une loi électorale lui permettant de rester à la tête du pays jusqu’au scrutin présidentiel du 22 décembre, pour lequel il est candidat probable. Mais le gouvernement n’a pratiquement pas mis en œuvre les conditions préalables à la tenue des élections, fixées dans l’accord de paix de 2018.

Le Rwanda et la Belgique rétablissent leurs relations diplomatiques, après une rupture liée au conflit en RDC. Kigali avait mis fin, en mars 2025, à ses relations diplomatiques avec Bruxelles, l’accusant d’avoir pris parti pour Kinshasa dans le conflit en République démocratique du Congo.

Au Maroc, des élections législatives marquées par la fracture sociale. Au pouvoir depuis 2021, les trois partis de la majorité s’entredéchirent, alors que les Marocains sont appelés aux urnes, mercredi 23 septembre.

En Afrique du Sud, 11 morts dans l’attaque d’une maison à Durban ; le pays « en état de choc et de deuil ». Trois personnes ont survécu à l’attaque, dont on ignore encore le mobile. L’Afrique du Sud affiche l’un des taux d’homicides les plus élevés au monde, avec environ 60 personnes tuées chaque jour dans un pays d’environ 63 millions d’habitants.

« Le Liberia ? J’ai d’abord pensé que c’était le nom d’un autre Etat américain » : la stupéfaction de migrants sud-américains expulsés en Afrique par Trump. Des citoyens sud-américains rencontrés par « Le Monde » disent avoir subi des violences physiques de la part des agents des services américains de l’immigration et des douanes présents à bord de l’avion qui les menaient au Liberia. Le pays s’est engagé à accueillir jusqu’à 1 200 personnes expulsées des Etats-Unis au cours des douze prochains mois.

CPI : un chef rebelle centrafricain reconnu coupable de crimes contre l’humanité. La Cour pénale internationale a établi que Mahamat Saïd Abdel Kani a supervisé des passages à tabac et des mauvais traitements lorsqu’il dirigeait l’Office central de répression du banditisme, une unité spéciale de police.

En Ethiopie, les rebelles du Tigré disent repousser une « invasion » des forces fédérales. Les Forces de défense tigréennes ont, par ailleurs, pris le contrôle de l’aéroport de Makalé, capitale de l’Etat. Trois jours plus tôt, sept mouvements actifs dans différentes régions du pays avaient annoncé la création d’une alliance pour renverser les autorités fédérales.

Au Mali, l’amertume des militaires en première ligne contre les djihadistes. Le 10 septembre, l’armée malienne a subi l’un de ses pires revers : au moins 100 soldats sont morts dans l’attaque du camp de Dioura par le GSIM. Une défaite qui met à nouveau sous pression le chef de la junte.

« Il faut être motivé pour voter » : au Maroc, les élections législatives sous la menace d’une abstention élevée. Le taux de participation est l’enjeu majeur du scrutin de mercredi, alors que la coalition gouvernementale sortante cherche à conforter sa majorité.

Rwanda et Belgique aplanissent leur différend sur la guerre en RDC et scellent leur réconciliation. En marge de l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies, Bruxelles et Kigali ont annoncé rétablir leurs relations diplomatiques, dix-huit mois après une rupture décidée par le Rwanda, qui accusait la Belgique de prendre partie contre lui dans le conflit qui ravage l’est de la République démocratique du Congo.

Former Barcelona midfielder and coach Xavi Hernandez has become the first foreigner in charge of the Dutch national team since the 1978 World Cup. Son of Israel’s US envoy injured in West Bank ramming attack. An Israeli soldier was seriously injured in a car-ramming incident in the occupied West Bank, with the attacker killed by troops at the scene.

Former Mexico boss Aguirre returns to Spain with Valencia. Javier Aguirre, former coach of the Mexican national team, has been appointed as the new head coach of Valencia in Spain’s La Liga. He previously led Real Mallorca to the Copa del Rey final.

Weinstein resentenced to 15 years in prison for 2006 sex assault. Harvey Weinstein, the former Hollywood producer, has been resentenced to 15 years for a 2006 sexual assault. This adds to his previous sentence of 23 years for other convictions.

US will honor defense commitments to Saudi Arabia, Rubio says. NEW YORK: The US will honor its defense commitments to Saudi Arabia, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday amid escalating regional tensions and Houthi attacks on the Kingdom. “We have a very strong defense agreement with Saudi Arabia, and we will live up to our commitments in that agreement,” Rubio told reporters when asked whether President Donald Trump was prepared to take further action against the Houthis. Rubio declined to discuss what military options were available to Trump

Russia probes bear attacks, as official says town under ‘siege’. At least six individuals have been killed by bear attacks in Siberia, prompting investigations into local negligence. An official reported that a town is effectively under ‘siege’ by the animals.

Zelensky, at UN, urges leaders to keep choking Russia’s revenues and impede its war efforts. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy appeals to world leaders at the UN General Assembly to target Russia’s revenues in order to curtail its war efforts.
Baltic states seek more EU funds for anti-drone defences. The Baltic states have requested additional EU funds for anti-drone defense amid concerns over potential hybrid attacks from Russia.

Klopp calls on Germany to ‘rise above ourselves’ as new era begins. Jurgen Klopp, newly appointed as Germany’s national football coach, encourages the team to harness collective strength ahead of facing the Netherlands. Germany is looking to recover from recent World Cup eliminations.

Libya to seek UN Security Council seat in 2028. Libya has announced its intention to seek Africa’s seat on the UN Security Council for the 2028 term, with Chairman Mohamed Al-Menfi emphasizing the country's commitment to international peace and justice. During his address at the UN General Assembly, he condemned violence in the Middle East and supported regional stability, while calling for cooperation among nations to address shared challenges. Al-Menfi portrayed Libya as a central player in the security and prosperity of Africa, and urged for a focus on sovereignty and accountability within the nation.

Venezuelan shot by ICE needs urgent medical care, mother tells AFP. A Venezuelan man shot by US ICE agents in Austin, Texas, needs urgent medical care due to a bullet near his spine. The shooting occurred during a DoorDash delivery.

AI leaders warn UN of security risks as systems grow more powerful. AI industry leaders have briefed the UN Security Council on the emerging risks posed by advanced AI technologies, highlighting differences between the US and China on regulatory approaches.

Europeans warn of rising Russian sabotage but see no imminent NATO attack. UNITED NATIONS: Russia is intensifying sabotage, cyberattacks and other hybrid attacks across Europe to undermine support for Ukraine, European ministers said, while dismissing concerns ​that Moscow is capable of launching a direct assault on NATO. Saudi Embassy in Georgia hosts reception to mark National Day. The Saudi Embassy in Georgia hosted a reception in the capital, Tbilisi, to mark National Day, the Saudi Press Agency reported on Wednesday. Saudi Ambassador to Georgia Salman Al-Sheikh welcomed Georgian Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Alexander Khvtisiashvili, ambassadors from friendly countries and Georgian government officials. Embassy staff and Saudi students studying in Georgia also attended the reception.

Indonesia brings heritage designs to Saudi Arabia’s biggest fashion expo. JAKARTA: Indonesian designers will present modern interpretations of heritage textiles at Saudi Fashiontex Expo, the Gulf region’s biggest fashion exhibition, as they seek to enter the Kingdom’s booming luxury and modest clothing sectors. Saudi Arabia is hosting more than 500 exhibitors from 25 countries and expecting over 10,000 international visitors for the fourth edition in Jeddah, which opens on Thursday. Outgoing UN chief makes final climate push at New York summit. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres focused on renewable energy’s growth and the need for countries to transition from fossil fuels at his final climate summit.

Zelensky says Putin using fighters from 47 countries in Ukraine war. UNITED NATIONS, United States: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin of using third-country fighters from 47 countries to prosecute Moscow’s war against Ukraine. A new geophysical survey of Tutankhamun’s tomb — known as KV62 — in the Valley of the Kings, published earlier in September in Nature, points to the possible existence of hidden corridors and chambers behind the burial chamber. England soccer great Harry Kane muses on future double duty playing in both NFL and MLS. Harry Kane, currently playing for Bayern Munich, has expressed interest in balancing a career in both the NFL as a kicker and joining Major League Soccer in the United States.

Marsh to stay on as Aussie skipper for opening ODI against South Africa. Retired Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood appointed first head of Makkah Defence Alliance secretariat. The Foreign Office (FO) announced on Wednesday that retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood had been appointed as the first secretary general of the Makkah Defence Alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. “The government of Pakistan is pleased to announce the appointment of Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood, Hilal-i-Imtiaz (Military), (retired), as the first secretary general pursuant to the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement,” the FO said in a handout, referring to the alliance’s initial name. “The secretary general will lead the general secretariat of the alliance being established at Riyadh,” the FO said. The agreement — signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on August 7 — empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all. Its inaugural meeting was held on Aug 31, where officials from all member states met in Istanbul to establish the institutional structure of the alliance and Pakistan was picked to head its secretariat in Riyadh. Under the decisions taken during the meeting, a secretariat headed by a secretary general will be established in Saudi Arabia to support the alliance’s work under the agreement. The secretariat will initially be headed by a secretary general from Pakistan for three years. The three countries also agreed to take steps to further institutionalise their cooperation in a manner that would enhance their solidarity, ensure the credibility and effectiveness of their collective deterrence and defence, and contribute to regional efforts and cooperative security towards a just, inclusive and lasting peace. Since its signing, there has been conversation about the possibility of its expansion, with Turkiye initially suggesting the possibility of Egypt’s inclusion. Though there has been no confirmation from Cairo. From Pakistan, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar clarified soon after the signing that the pact was defensive in nature, with the latter saying that it was also “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles. However, when Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan was asked about possibility of the pact’s expansion during a weekly media briefing on Sept 10, he said an expansion was not on the cards at that point. The three countries first needed to solidify the new organisation before considering opening it to other states with similar threat perceptions and requirements, he explained. Meanwhile, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said last week that the alliance has no “regional aspirations”, adding that it was intended for collective deterrence. Meanwhile, as the US-Iran conflict continues to expand with Yemen’s Houthi rebels attacking Saudi Arabia, he also said that Pakistan would go to “any extent” to defend Saudi Arabia, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security was “unconditional”.

Punjab govt seeks Rangers deployment in Rawalpindi, three other districts until Oct 5. The Punjab government has requested the federal government to deploy Rangers in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali districts from Sept 22 to Oct 5 to assist the provincial police in maintaining law and order amid an expected protest on Sept 27. The request comes as the Kissan Ittehad and PTI have announced long marches and sit-ins in Islamabad in the coming week. PTI has announced a long march on Sept 27 to press for the release of its founder, Imran Khan. The letter, a copy of which is available with Dawn , said Rangers had been requested for deployment in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali from Sept 22 to Oct 5. According to a letter sent by the Punjab Home Department to the Ministry of Interior and Narcotics Control, three companies of the Pakistan Rangers have been sought for deployment in Rawalpindi, including one for Rawalpindi city and two for Taxila. Five Rangers wings have been sought for Attock, while Jhelum and Mianwali have each been allocated one company. The deployment is proposed under Article 245 of the Constitution of Pakistan, 1973, Sections 4 and 5 of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, and Sections 7(b) and 10 of the Pakistan Rangers Ordinance, 1959. The letter said the matter was discussed threadbare at the 59th meeting of the Standing Committee of the Cabinet on Law & Order (SCCLO) of the Punjab government, held on Sept 20. The meeting considered the situational review presented by police authorities, the orders of the Islamabad High Court (IHC) in Writ Petition No. 4421/2026, and instructions issued by the S&GAD, Government of Punjab, through a letter dated Sept 19, 2026, it stated. “After due consideration, it was authorised that the requisition be sent to the ministry of interior, for requisition of troops ensuring law and order in the districts mentioned above,” the letter stated. The letter asked the ministry to take further necessary action and intimate the Punjab Home Department accordingly. Section 144 declared Separately, Section 144 has been enforced across Punjab for 13 days, with a complete ban imposed on the assembly, processions, or gathering of five or more people in public places, on highways, or in open spaces across Punjab. Inciting people to unlawful assembly is also prohibited. The ban does not apply, however, to wedding ceremonies, funeral prayers, burials, or gatherings at mosques and other places of worship. Courts of law, government or semi-governmental organisations’ official duties, and events held with official permission from the deputy commissioner of the concerned district are also exempt. A complete ban has also been imposed on carrying or displaying weapons of any kind in public places, according to an order issued by the Punjab Home Department. This ban exempts personnel of law enforcement agencies (LEAs), intelligence agencies (IAs) and security agencies on official duty. The order, a copy of which is available with Dawn , said that Section 144 was imposed in view of serious threats to public peace, tranquillity, and the lives and property of citizens across Punjab. “Multiple threat alerts have been received from IAs regarding possible terrorist activities being planned by such hostile agencies by employing suicide bombers, Vehicle-Borne Improvised Explosive Devices (VBIEDs) and target killings during large public gatherings across Punjab to create mayhem, social unrest and disrupt public peace and tranquillity,” it said, noting that “gatherings, rallies, public meetings, sit-ins, processions, and demonstrations” could become potential soft targets for terrorist attacks. The order has been enforced immediately and is to remain in effect for 13 days. In addition, the department also sent a letter to the interior ministry requesting mobile and internet services at specific locations in Rawalpindi and Attock to be downgraded or jammed on Sept 27 due to the “expected law and order situation”. The letter asked for 2G, 3G and 4G networks to be jammed at specified locations in Rawalpindi city, which it said would be communicated later. It also requested the same for Barahma Bahtar to M-1, Gango, Ahata, Taxila City, Wah Saddar, Thalian, and Chakri. It also requested to downgrade mobile and internet services throughout Attock district. The decision to disrupt mobile and internet signals was made at the request of police to maintain law and order, according to the Home Department. Preparations in the Rawalpindi Division and the federal capital territory to maintain security and deal with any emergency situation are in full swing in light of the potential long march by the PTI and other protests in Islamabad. More than 22,000 security personnel led by eight DIGs will be deployed in the federal capital and over 30,000 in the Attock district, which connects Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with Punjab. In Aug, the federal government authorised the deployment of three companies of the Pakistan Army in Rawalpindi for six months to perform “sensitive security duties” and respond to any unforeseen situation. The deployment was approved more than a month before the planned PTI march towards Islamabad. The party claims that the Sept 27 long march could draw around two million participants. District administrations in Punjab have previously sought army assistance under Article 245 during Muharram, election periods, and times of heightened terror alerts. With the deployment approved for an initial period of six months “with immediate effect”, the army units will be placed at the disposal of the Rawalpindi district administration and will perform duties as assigned by the civilian authorities.

'Breaking Bad' inspired teenager arrested in Bahawalpur for allegedly attempting to poison father with AI help. LAHORE: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Wednesday arrested a 17-year-old student from Bahawalpur for allegedly attempting to poison his father, after seeking guidance from artificial intelligence (AI) on how to administer a potentially fatal substance. A spokesperson for the agency said that according to preliminary information, the suspect — a second-year student and the only son of his parents — had reportedly developed strained relations with his father and allegedly planned to kill him following a disagreement. During the investigation, authorities learned that the teenager had developed an interest in chemistry after watching the American crime drama ‘Breaking Bad’. He had reportedly set up a small laboratory at home to conduct chemical experiments, the spokesperson said. The suspect allegedly obtained chemical material from Australia and Islamabad and concocted a substance at home with the intention of poisoning his father. He reportedly administered the substance to his father on one occasion, but the attempt was not successful, the spokesperson said. Subsequently, the teenager allegedly sought further guidance from AI, asking how to administer a poison capable of causing his father’s death without detection, he added. The spokesperson said the Punjab NCCIA received the information about the suspect through an automated system. Following this, NCCIA Punjab Director Hissam Bin Iqbal directed the formation of a team to investigate the matter. The team later conducted an operation in Bahawalpur and arrested the suspect. Further investigation was under way to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident, the nature of the chemicals involved and the suspect’s online activities, the spokesperson said. AI chatbots and agents have been linked to cases of harm and death, leading to concerns about their usage and the imposition of tighter regulations and controls. The Euro­pean Union last month introduced sweeping laws that give it the power to enfo­rce landmark AI rules and to fine any companies that break the law. Pakistan has also previously called for the use of AI to be regulated by the United Nations charter. Last year, American artificial intelligence firm OpenAI said it would add parental controls to its chatbot ChatGPT after an American couple said the system had encouraged their teenage son to kill himself.

Staging protests a legal and constitutional right, says KP CM ahead of PTI's Sept 27 long march. Ahead of the PTI’s planned long march to Islamabad on Sept 27, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said on Wednesday that staging a protest was a legal and constitutional right. Addressing a cabinet meeting in Peshawar, CM Afridi alleged that for the past three to four days, “plainclothes individuals” had been targeting PTI workers, office-bearers and elected representatives. He alleged that an assassination attempt was made on Communications and Works Minister Shakil Khan, who also managed to evade an attempt to abduct him. CM Afridi further alleged that Minister for Public Health Engineering Fazal Shakoor was abducted by plainclothes individuals, who also opened fire on his car. “If a minister, a provincial cabinet member is not safe from these thugs, then what about the common man?” he asked. The chief minister emphasised that the treatment being meted out to provincial cabinet members was “unacceptable”. “These people are afraid of the power of the people. No sane person would take such measures,” he asserted. He also assailed PML-N’s Rana Sanaullah’s reported remarks labelling the people of KP as terrorists and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz remarks regarding the terror threat from other provinces . He said that from today, the province would be cut off from the rest of Pakistan and all routes to it would be closed. “The rest of Pakistan will remain open, but no one will be able to enter or leave KP,” he said. “What should we make of cutting KP off from the rest of Pakistan and closing all routes? Is there a conspiracy underway? Is an attempt being made to repeat the East Pakistan tragedy?” he asked. “Whatever conspiracy is being hatched, and whoever is behind it, our clear message to them is: Pakistan belongs to us,” the chief minister said. He asserted that KP was and will continue to be a part of Pakistan. “Goons dressed in plain clothes are intimidating and threatening our bureaucracy, police, deputy commissioners and district police officers,” he further alleged. The chief minister advised that the bureaucracy, police, deputy commissioners and district police officers to not to be afraid. “If the provincial government is not asking you to do anything wrong, do not obey unlawful orders from any institution or department,” he said. “Protesting is everyone’s legal and constitutional right. We will stage a peaceful protest because we are not being heard anywhere … the Constitution allows us to hold peaceful protests, and we will protest at all cost,” he said. “As long as the right to peaceful protest exists in the Constitution, we will continue to hold peaceful protests,” CM Afridi maintained. “My message to the people of KP and the entire Pakistan is: do not panic, do not be afraid,” he said. Preparations in the Rawalpindi Division and the federal capital territory to maintain security and deal with any emergency situation are in full swing in light of the potential long march by the PTI and other protests in Islamabad. Earlier this week, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had warned the PTI against its long march, urging the party to refrain from proceeding with the protest. The interior minister vowed the government will not “leave any loopholes” in its response if the party went ahead with the protest.

Mir Raza murder case: Judicial commission notes motives of MLO who conducted first postmortem 'appear tainted'. KARACHI: A judicial commission investigating the circumstances and possible negligence in the Mir Raza Ali murder case has observed that the motives of Medico-Legal Officer (MLO) Dr Osama Sheikh, who conducted the first autopsy, “appear tainted”. The body of the 25-year-old businessman was found in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar on July 29, a day after he went missing. After his family accused the police of trying to bury the facts, a judicial commission has been holding regular hearings to probe the circumstances and possible negligence in the murder case. During Tuesday’s hearing, Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed accused MLO Sheikh of instigating a “malicious campaign” against her after she had disputed the findings of Ali’s first post-mortem. According to a written order for the hearing issued on Wednesday, Dr Syed had submitted a “letter coupled with a number of documents as evidence of the malicious campaign launched against her on the instigation” of Dr Sheikh. The one-member commission, headed by Sindh High Court’s (SHC) Justice Omar Sial, noted that Dr Sheikh’s “motives and intentions appear tainted”. “His conduct has attempted to damage the honour of this commission and to detract from and scandalise its real purpose.” Justice Sial wrote that he was saddened to see the police surgeon request the commission “in a very graceful, polite and professional manner” to take notice of the “highly defamatory and dangerous social media campaign against her”. Dr Syed informed the commission that she was under “immense mental anguish and that the material being circulated against her had set a very dangerous precedent that no senior henceforth should attempt to help rectify mistakes done by the junior for fear of prosecution”, the order stated. The commission noted that Dr Syed was a distinguished and seasoned professional with an impressive academic and work background, and her being subjected to such harassment was “unacceptable”. “She is an asset to the government. Rather than appreciate her services, she is being defamed.” Dr Syed had also told the commission at a previous hearing that she faced “threats” after disputing the findings of the first postmortem. In its order, the commission requested the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency’s (NCCIA) Karachi director to investigate the issue of a message exchange between the police surgeon and Dr Sheikh. It also urged the NCCIA to identify whether the defamatory messages circulating on the internet were “forensically satisfactory”, and determine who was responsible for the leakage of these messages on the internet. It directed the NCCIA Karachi director to submit a comprehensive report to the commission before the end of its tenure. During his previous appearance before the commission on Sept 1, the MLO had told the judicial commission that he was not under any influence or pressure while conducting the postmortem and had nowhere stated in his report that Ali had died by suicide. For its part, the commission had expressed dissatisfaction with Dr Sheikh’s answers, questioned the discrepancies between his initial and final reports and asked whether he or a sweeper had conducted the autopsy. He had maintained that he had conducted the procedure and that the final report was issued after the exhumation and second autopsy, following 14 objections by the police surgeon. In a hearing on Monday, the commission also declined the MLO’s request to record a further statement, observing that he “appeared on social media” and said that he had “more to tell the commission than what he told it earlier”. Tuesday’s hearing In its Tuesday hearing, the commission recorded the statements of Abid Farooq Sumar, Asif Farooq Sumar, Faizur Rehman and Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASF) Nida Junaid. The statement of witness Sarim bin Tahir has also been recorded through Zoom. The commission issued notices to Sindh Health Department Secretary Tahir Hussain Sangi, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Samiullah Soomro and Provincial Emergency Operation Centre Secretary Shehryar Memon for their appearance on Thursday at 11am. Memon has recently been appointed as the Sindh health services director general to replace Dr Pervez Ahmed Shaikh — a decision taken by the Sindh government on the day the latter testified before the commission and named Memon as the person who issued instructions to change the medical board formed for exhuming Ali’s body. Notices were also issued to Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) and Investigation Officer (IO) Siraj Ahmed Lashari and CPLC Assistant Chief (Operations/Complaint Resolution Centre) Kashif Iftikhar for their appearance on Sept 28 (Monday) at 11am. According to the order, during Tuesday’s hearing, Ali’s family said they believed another special medical board was being considered. The family did not get any reply upon approaching Deputy Inspector General Amir Farooqi for confirmation. In his order, Justice Sial further observed that if the Ali family’s information was correct, such a move would nullify the commission’s work to date. “The commission will then be unable to give its conclusive findings. It will narrow the commission’s terms. The Government of Sindh has incurred substantial expenses in running this commission,” Justice Sial wrote. The absence of “reliable, efficient, and complete communication” between the deceased’s family and the police was fueling public speculation, the judge noted. The commission requested the Sindh inspector general (IG) that a duly authorised police focal person be appointed to communicate with the family and provide official information to the press and media. The judicial panel noted that the witness statement again revealed that the entire record had not been provided to it. “Even after repeated reminders, such a lack of relevant records is regrettable,” the order said.

19 terrorists killed, soldier martyred in operations in Balochistan: ISPR. Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Wednesday that 19 terrorists had been killed and a soldier was martyred in several operations across Balochistan. In a statement, it said intelligence agencies had reported the presence of multiple hideouts of Indian-sponsored Fitna al Khawarij and Fitna al Hindustan in Quetta district’s Shaban area “posing a threat to the local population”. The state uses the term Fitna al Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and refers to designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. “In order to safeguard the local populace and clear the area of terrorists, security forces have been conducting a clearance operation in the general area of Shaban since Sept 21. During the operation, security forces effectively engaged and cleared multiple terrorist hideouts,” it said. “Following an intense exchange of fire, 13 Indian-sponsored terrorists have been killed so far. Weapons, ammunition and explosives were also recovered from the cleared hideouts. The clearance operation will continue until the complete neutralisation of the threat in the area,” it said. The ISPR statement went on to say that security forces also conducted “pre-emptive intelligence-based operations” in Kech and Quetta West, during separate engagements on Sept 22 and 23. “During the operations, troops effectively engaged the terrorists and, following an intense exchange of fire, six terrorists were killed,” it said, adding that weapons and ammunition were also recovered. It said that 39-year-old Subedar Muhammad Jamil, a resident of Taunsa Sharif, embraced martyrdom during the exchange of fire. The statement said that the counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of ‘Azm-i-Istehkam’ would continue at full pace. “Security forces and law enforcement agencies remain committed to eliminating the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” it concluded. President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the security forces for their successful operations. In a statement, he said that the elimination of Indian-backed terrorists was a testament to the professionalism of the security forces. President Zardari also paid tribute to Subedar Jamil, saying that his sacrifice was a symbol of the security forces’ unwavering commitment to the nation’s peace and security. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also hailed the successful operations. “We commend the courage and professional capabilities of the security forces for killing 19 terrorists,” Naqvi said, adding that operations against those disrupting the peace in Balochistan were ongoing. Earlier in the day, Radio Pakistan had reported that security forces killed two terrorists affiliated with Fitna al Hindustan during an intelligence-based operation in the Jausak area of Turbat. Pakistan Television had also reported that security forces continued operations against terrorists in Balochistan under Raddul Fitna-3. In Mastung, nine terrorists were killed after they attempted to attack a checkpost, according to the state broadcaster. Heavy weapons, ammunition and three motorcycles were also recovered, it added. “Operations will continue until the threat is eliminated,” Pakistan TV said, quoting the security forces. Terrorists killed in gun battle with police Meanwhile, Balochistan police killed five terrorists in a gun battle in Quetta’s Aghbarg area after terrorists attempted to attack a police station, officials said. Officials said the terrorists targeted the Aghbarg police station, located on the outskirts of Quetta, in the early hours of Wednesday. Police personnel deployed at the station immediately returned fire. “In a heavy exchange of fire, five terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan were killed by police,” Saddar Senior Superintendent of Police Shafqat Janjua said. He added that police had foiled the attack and seized weapons and ammunition. According to Janjua, the attackers arrived in the area on motorcycles before targeting the police station. Separately, the Edhi Foundation said one of its ambulances was allegedly hijacked by armed men in Balochistan on Wednesday. In a statement, the foundation said the ambulance was returning to the Edhi Kalat Centre at around 7:15am after transporting the body of a woman from an area near Gidar, about 110 kilometres from Civil Hospital, Kalat. The foundation said unidentified armed men assaulted the Edhi worker and took control of the ambulance. On Tuesday, Radio Pakistan reported that six terrorists were killed and nine suspected individuals were arrested during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) by security forces in Balochistan’s Saran Tangi area. On Monday, security forces killed four more terrorists belonging to a banned organisation in an intelligence-based operation carried out in two areas of Panjgur district. Last week, security forces killed 11 terrorists in separate operations in Panjgur and Chagai districts. The number of terrorist attacks in the province increased by seven per cent from 83 in July to 89 in August, according to a monthly assessment by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies.

Pezeshkian says Iran will not surrender after Trump's annihilation threat. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said in a speech at the United Nations on Wednesday that Tehran would never surrender to the United States but still believes in diplomacy, a day after US President Donald Trump used the same forum to threaten to “annihilate” Iran. The duelling speeches at the annual UN General Assembly in New York bookended the first shuttle talks between the US and Iran for months, which appeared to have yielded no concessions in the public stance of either side towards ending the Middle East war . In his speech, Pezeshkian defended Iran’s military actions as defensive, and insisted Iran was not seeking nuclear weapons. The president struck a defiant tone speaking at the UN for the first time since Washington and Israel launched an all-out war on his country, vowing Tehran would never “bend at the knee”. Pezeshkian accused Washington of “terrorism” for assassinating former supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei at the start of the war. He held up a photograph of the dead leader, before insisting Tehran had never started a war. On Tuesday, Trump had told the UN he was weighing whether to “annihilate” Iran, but went on to hail renewed talks between Tehran and Washington’s negotiators. Pezeshkian made no reference to the talks to resolve the stalled war in his steely speech. “(Trump) must know that the resistance of the Iranian people will only increase in the face of sanctions, increased pressure, increased bullying. We will never bow our head or bend at the knee,” he said. Pezeshkian insisted that Tehran would not allow the Strait of Hormuz, which it has been intermittently blockaded since the start of the war causing global energy prices to spike, to be used for aggression against his country. “We cannot let some have free access and bolster their interests from the waterway, while at the same time using that waterway to impose their aggression upon us,” he said. Soaring fuel prices threaten to cost Trump’s Republicans their control of Congress in November’s midterms. Pezeshkian’s attendance at the UN’s signature diplomatic event, in the heart of Manhattan, had been in doubt as it was unclear if the United States would issue a visa. Ultimately Washington granted the permit, but denied visas to several members of Pezeshkian’s entourage. Indirect contact The annual UN gathering in New York provided the occasion on Tuesday for Iranian and US officials to hold their first known indirect talks since a ceasefire collapsed in July, with Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner communicating through mediators on the sidelines. “Steve and Jared had a very productive meeting today with mediators of Iran,” Trump said on Tuesday after his own speech. “I think there’s a lot of momentum for them to make a deal. It’s what we’re hearing from everybody.” Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baqaei said Tehran had engaged with Washington through a Qatari mediator and conveyed conditions, including an end to the war on all fronts and a halt to US “acts of aggression”. Some Iranian state media initially reported that Araghchi and Witkoff had met , but Iranian officials clarified to Reuters that it was not face-to-face. The diplomatic contact in New York caused a backlash in Iranian media associated with hardliners. An opinion piece run by the semi-official Tasnim news agency, associated with the Revolutionary Guards, said Araghchi was wrong to have contacts with Witkoff and Kushner, “a major gift to Trump”, as Iran had already conveyed its terms. Iranian sources told Reuters the delegation had been ordered not to meet the Americans face-to-face by the Supreme National Security Council, a body that includes figures selected by Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, the supreme leader.

Abrar Ahmed rises to No. 1 in ICC T20I bowling rankings. Pakistan’s Abrar Ahmed has risen to the top of the ICC Men’s T20I bowling rankings for the first time in his career, ending Afghanistan leg-spinner Rashid Khan’s six-month reign at No. 1. Abrar moved to the summit after Rashid slipped one rating point behind the Pakistan spinner’s tally of 736 following an unimpressive outing against India. The 28-year-old became only the fifth Pakistan bowler to top the T20I bowling rankings, following Umar Gul, Saeed Ajmal, Imad Wasim and Shahid Afridi. Abrar, who has played 10 Tests, 19 ODIs and 38 T20Is for Pakistan, has taken 133 international wickets. He is also ranked second in the ODI bowling rankings, 39 rating points behind Rashid, who occupies the top position in that format. The Karachi-born right-arm mystery spinner has featured in nine T20Is for Pakistan this year and taken 15 wickets, including six in the three-match home series against Australia, which Pakistan won 3-0 in January and February. Abrar said the achievement fulfilled a long-held ambition of his. “When you start playing cricket, you have only one dream to represent Pakistan. Once you achieve that, the next dream is to become world number one,” he was quoted as saying by the Pakistan Cricket Board’s digital platform. “I feel very proud to become the world number one bowler while representing Pakistan. I will continue working hard to achieve more success and win more matches for Pakistan.” Abrar said improving his consistency had been a particular focus of his work. “In the past, I had variations in my bowling, but consistency was an area I needed to improve. I worked hard on my consistency and that work has helped me improve a lot,” he said. He is currently with Pakistan’s Asian Games squad, which is undergoing a four-day training camp in Karachi ahead of the competition in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. “My aim is to perform well and help my team win matches and return to Pakistan with a gold medal,” Abrar said.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs390.12 per litre while HSD will cost Rs414.75 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable for Sept 24 (Thursday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

Section 144 imposed in Islamabad; district admin warns citizens against participating in any 'illegal activity'. Section 144 has been imposed for two months in Islamabad, it emerged on Wednesday, with the district administration warning citizens against participating in any “illegal activity”. The order comes as the Kissan Ittehad and PTI have announced long marches and sit-ins in Islamabad in the coming week. The PTI has announced a long march on Sept 27 to press for the release of its founder, Imran Khan, who is currently incarcerated in Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail. A copy of the order, issued by Islamabad Additional District Magistrate Dr Anam Fatima and dated Sept 18, is available with Dawn . According to the order, Section 144 of the Criminal Procedure Code has been enforced with immediate effect and “shall remain in force for a period of two months”. The order prohibited gatherings of five or more people, as well as processions, rallies and demonstrations, at any public place within the revenue limits of the district, including the Red Zone. Highlighting that “certain segments of society” were planning to organise “unlawful assemblies”, the order termed it “necessary to control such types of illegal activities which present a threat to public peace, tranquillity and maintenance of law and order”. It added that processions and demonstrations being planned in the territory were likely to threaten public peace, cause annoyance and injury, endanger human life and safety, threaten public property and could lead to a riot in Islamabad. On these grounds, it stated that “immediate prevention and speedy remedy is required” to protect life and property. In a separate statement issued on Wednesday, the district administration said that Section 144 had been enforced in the federal capital. “No gatherings or assemblies of any kind are permitted in the city. Gatherings are also banned under the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act 2024,” the district administration said. It said that strict legal action will be taken in the event of a violation, adding that violation of the act carried a penalty of three years’ imprisonment. “Citizens are urged not to participate in any illegal activity, and to cooperate with security agencies and demonstrate responsibility,” it added. Preparations in the Rawalpindi Division and the federal capital territory to maintain security and deal with any emergency situation are in full swing in light of the potential long march by the PTI and other protests in Islamabad. Section 144 has also separately been enforced across Punjab for 13 days, in view of “serious threats” to public peace, tranquillity, and the lives and property of citizens across Punjab. The Punjab government has also requested the federal government to deploy Rangers in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali districts from Sept 22 to Oct 5 to assist the provincial police in maintaining law and order amid the expected protest on Sept 27. In August, the federal government authorised the deployment of three companies of the Pakistan Army in Rawalpindi for six months to perform “sensitive security duties” and respond to any unforeseen situation.

FBR notifies new tax rules for non-resident influencers. ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has introduced new rules to tax income earned from social media content, targeting non-resident Pakistanis. The new tax rules will target all those individuals who generate income through user interactions in Pakistan. The new rules were notified through a notification, SRO 1642 of 2026, released on Wednesday. In the budget, the government had introduced a five per cent tax rate on social media content earnings. Under the new rules, anyone earning money from social media content will be taxed if their audience crosses a certain size. The threshold has been set at more than 50,000 users in a year or 12,250 users in a quarter. Regulations will target individuals who generate income through social media user interactions in Pakistan Tax officials have begun identifying high-earning social media accounts with millions of followers that have remained outside the tax net. The move comes at a time when social media has emerged as a major source of income, with earnings running into millions annually. The race for maximum followers is no longer about fame or status, but about monetising platforms to earn money through digital content. Unlike traditional earnings from trade or services, income on social media is largely generated through audience engagement and viewership. For those who qualify for taxation, the minimum taxable income will be calculated by taking the total earnings from social media and subtracting expenses, which can be claimed only up to 30 per cent of revenue. Under the rules, the remuneration is defined as the higher of actual earnings or revenue-per-mille (fixed at Rs195 per 1,000 views on YouTube, subject to revision). The individuals will pay advance tax quarterly and declare income in a special section of their annual return. Commissioners are empowered to rectify under-declarations. According to the rules, the higher of either the assessed income or remuneration received by a person from their social media content, whether in cash or kind, will be considered taxable income. The rules also define that a social media platform means an internet-based service whose primary purpose is to enable users to interact with other users and share user-generated content, where the economic value of the service arises from user participation, network effects, and the monetisation of user engagement or user data. It further said that social media content means any digital information, communication, or creative material generated or published by a user on a social media platform, the value of which arises from user engagement, audience reach, or platform-facilitated dissemination, including content capable of generating advertising, sponsorship or other monetisation revenue. ‘Carrot and stick’ dangled before PTI ahead of march. • Message conveyed to party that capital protest will not be allowed, come what may • Party cadres remain in the dark, as CM Afridi expected to unveil strategy tomorrow • Insiders say govt has offered to shift Imran, Bushra out of prison, allow meeting with family if march is called off • Minister denies offering any ‘confidence-building measures’ ISLAMABAD: The PTI, which is expected to come out with its plan for the Sept 27 protest by tomorrow (Friday), has been told that the federal government will not allow it to go through with the planned march on Islamabad, Dawn has learnt. Discussions with leaders privy to developments suggest that the party has been offered certain confidence-building measures (CBMs) in backchannel contacts with the powers that be. However, the party has also been conveyed “in clear terms” that it would not be allowed to march on the capital, and that preparations are in place to ‘fix them for good’ in case they do go ahead with the protest. PTI insiders claimed that as part of the supposed CBMs, the government had offered to shift former prime minister Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi to Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) and Banigala, respectively. Similarly, sources said government representatives had told them that Mr Khan’s family members could be allowed to meet him in hospital, but not before Sept 27 — as that could be construed as “weakness” on the government’s part. Insiders also claimed that the federal government had warned transporters that they would face the music, if they provided buses and vans to protesters. Following such warnings, some companies had already refused to provide the PTI with equipment such as cranes and heavy machinery, which the party has previously used to remove containers and other obstacles set up to block their path. PTI’s Naeem Haider Panjutha said the government had closed down Islamabad, and the PTI would come to re-open it, while following the orders of Islamabad High Court (IHC). When asked about their plans for the 27th, Mr Panjutha told Dawn that workers from west, central and south Punjab will protest in their respective areas. “However, workers from North Punjab will join the march led by CM Afridi,” he said, adding that the march would not be called off. When contacted, PTI spokesperson Sheikh Waqas Akram said their march would be totally peaceful and the party would not own any violence. He also suggested that the federal government engage opposition leaders Raja Nasir Abbas and Mehmood Khan Achakzai, as they had been authorised by Imran Khan to negotiate on the opposition’s behalf. Govt denies offering any CBMs When contacted, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry refuted the PTI claim that they had been offered any CBMs. “Had the government offered any confidence-building measures, there would have been no long march,” Mr Chaudhry told Dawn , adding that the party had made such “one-sided claims” in the past too, but they were not true. “They are claiming too much. We are not even prepared to offer them less,” he said. The minister also insisted that civilian law enforcement agencies were capable enough to handle the PTI threat, adding that the armed forces would not need to be called in. Uncertainty within the party A senior PTI leader said that KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi was expected to announce the long march plan on Friday. However, he admitted that so far, the leadership and workers in Punjab, Sindh and Balochistan have no clue about the strategy. “In the past, three convoys used to march from KP. When Ali Amin Gandapur led the march from Peshawar, a second group from Hazara was led by Omar Ayub, and third caravan from south KP was spearheaded by Umar Amin Gandapur,” one party leader recalled. At the time, Ali Amin would come via the Hazara Motorway alongside the Omar Ayub-led caravan, while Umar Amin’s people would take the CPEC route (M14). “Now it is being said that 12 caravans will leave from KP,” the party leader said. He expressed the fear that these marchers may even be stopped within KP, given the amount of influence the Centre was exerting over the provincial police force. Ministers’ homes are being raided; MNAs, MPAs and even union council leaders are being arrested. “For the last four days, a prominent minister has been residing in CM House to avoid arrest,” another party leader claimed. He revealed that on Tuesday night, KP high-ups called three police officers, but they refused to turn up, adding that this was one of the main reasons why the government was mulling curtailing police powers in the province. When asked why police was not heeding the KP government, he explained that Imran Khan had given wide powers to the provincial police force. “When Ali Amin was CM, he curtailed some of those powers, but during Sohail Afridi’s rule, the police department won a reprieve from the Peshawar High Court and became ‘independent’ again,” he said, adding that surprisingly, the provincial government did not even bother filing an appeal against the decision.” A Punjab based party leader recalled that previously, they were criticised for failing to mobilise supporters from the province, but this time around, it seemed that even party cadres in KP were facing similar problems. PM Shehbaz may meet Pezeshkian today. NEW YORK: Pakistan’s push to broker dialogue between Washington and Tehran appeared to be gathering pace on Wedne­sday, with diplomatic sou­rces suggesting a meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, could be on the cards today (Thursday). Meanwhile, PM Sheh­baz’s address to the UN General Assembly has been rescheduled to 12.30am (Pakistan time) on Friday. The anticipated engagement with the Iranian president comes as Isla­m­abad continues efforts to bring US and Iran back to the negotiating table. Diplomatic sources say Qatar is handling the immediate shuttle diplomacy between the US and Iran in New York, while Pakistan is working through a parallel channel with Tehran as regional efforts intensify to keep the latest diplomatic contacts from collapsing. The distinction has emerged from reporting by US and international media on the renewed US-Iran contacts around the United Nations General Assembly, with Qatar and Pakistan both involved in efforts to keep communication open between Washington and Tehran. The two countries, however, appear to be operating through different but connected channels. Qatar has been directly involved in the New York shuttle, with US special envoy Steve Witkoff saying mediators “shuttled between” the American and Iranian delegations during lengthy discussions on Tuesday. Qatar has also acknowledged working with Pakistan to reduce tensions between Washington and Tehran and to promote dialogue. Separately, PM Shehbaz met International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva on the sidelines of the assembly. The prime minister reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to the IMF-supported reform programme, citing progress in fiscal discipline, tariff regimes, and privatisation as the country transitions toward economic recovery despite regional turmoil. Nepra notifies KE base tariff at Rs32.37 per unit. • Revised tariff Rs7.60 lower than original Rs39.97 determination • KE says revised MYT financially unsustainable, may pursue legal remedies • Consumers will continue to pay uniform tariff applicable to other Discos ISLAMABAD: The National Electric Power Reg­ulatory Authority (Nepra) on Wednesday notified K-Electric’s average base tariff at Rs32.37 per unit under its seven-year multiyear tariff (MYT) regime for FY24 to FY30, effectively reducing the government’s subsidy burden by almost Rs200 billion. Nepra had originally determined KE’s multiyear tariff at Rs39.97 per unit for the period but revised it down by Rs7.60 per unit, or 19pc, to Rs32.37 in October last year on review petitions filed by the power division, Jamaat-i-Islami, Karachi-based industrialists and KE management on different grounds. The Rs32.37 base tariff for FY24 will be indexed to inflation and exchange-rate variations for the subsequent six years through FY30. Informed sources said the revised determination reduced KE’s effective rate of return to around 13-14pc from 22-23pc under the previous determination and cut subsidy payables by the government to K-Electric by around Rs200bn over the seven-year period. K-Electric had challenged Nepra’s revised MYT determination in the Sindh High Court and secured a stay against its implementation. The court later referred the matter to Nepra’s Appellate Tribunal, being the appropriate forum under the law. A three-member tribunal on Wedn­esday upheld Nepra’s revised determination and rejected KE’s position. Nepra subsequently issued four interrelated gazette notifications and clarified that KE consumers would not be charged the tariff determined by the regulator. Instead, they would continue to be cha­rged the uniform tariff applicable to consumers of other distribution companies, in line with the federal government’s policy guidelines of Aug 22, 2023, under the National Electricity Policy, 2021. The matter has now attained finality through the gazette notifications unless stayed or overturned by a higher legal forum, i.e. a high court, the Federal Constitutional Court or the Supreme Court of Pakistan as the case may be. A KE spokesperson indicated that the company could challenge the decision, saying the revised tariff was not financially sustainable. “In pursuance of the order of the Nepra Appellate Tribunal in the matter of appeals filed by K-Electric against Nepra’s decisions dated Oct 20, 2025, today a verbal order was announced where it was informed that K-Electric’s appeals have been dismissed. However, the written order is yet to be issued by the tribunal,” the spokesperson said. “This development has a substantial adverse impact on K-Electric’s Multi-Year Tariff for the control period FY2024 to FY2030 and is therefore not considered financially sustainable for the company,” the spokesperson added. KE said it would consider all legal remedies available to it after receiving the tribunal’s detailed order. The government had earlier challenged Nepra’s original Rs39.97 per unit base tariff, which was indexed to inflation and the exchange rate, arguing that it gave KE an undue benefit of almost Rs750bn over the seven-year control period at the expense of the national exchequer, consumers across the country and taxpayers. It had cited higher allowances for law and order, losses and fuel price adjustments, among other factors, compared to other distribution companies. Nepra had rejected some review petitions on technical grounds, including limitation and locus standi, but accepted several substantive points under its regulatory mandate to ensure legality, regulatory coherence and protection of public interest. The regulator said precedents showed that, where public interest warranted, it could revisit its own determinations despite procedural defects in applications filed by parties. It said previous determinations had recognised and exercised powers of self-review under the Nepra Act, Tariff Rules and Review Regulations to correct material errors and align outcomes with sector realities. “These decisions confirm that the authority’s power to review and correct its determinations in the interest of justice is not extinguished by procedural infirmities in the initiating pleadings”, it said.
